syllabusTopics: Introduction and characteristics of aromatic compounds
Preparation of benzene from decarboxylation of sodium benzoate, phenol, and ethyne only

Chemical properties of benzene: addition reactions (hydrogen, halogen); electrophilic substitution reactions: orientation of benzene derivatives (o, m and p), nitration, sulphonation, halogenation, Friedel-Crafts reaction (alkylation and acylation)
Combustion of benzene (free combustion only) and uses

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Kekulé's 1865 hexagon gave benzene its skeleton, its isomer counts, and its two contributing structures — and failed on three independent experiments: one bond length (139 pm) where it predicted two, 208 kJ/mol of hydrogenation where it predicted 360, and substitution where it predicted addition. Modern resonance theory keeps the two forms as equal contributors to a single hybrid, the circle-icon of every textbook.…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Kekulé's Structure: The Model That Almost Worked Kekulé (1865) proposed benzene as a cyclic hexagon with alternating single and double bonds — the first correct *skeleton* in organic chemistry. The structure explains the formula C₆H₆, the monosubstitution uniqueness, and even the o/m/p isomer pattern — but it fails on bond lengths, hydrogenation heat, and substitution chemistry.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **The proposal:** a six-membered ring with three alternating C=C and C–C bonds; two equivalent structures related by "breathing" (Kekulé's own oscillation story). - **What it explains:** C₆H₆ with tetravalent carbon; only one monosubstitution product (all six positions equivalent by symmetry); exactly three disubstitution patterns (ortho, meta, para).…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: A model's failures are as informative as its successes - three independent experiments falsify simple alternation and point to delocalisation.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Kekule 1865: cyclic hexagon, alternating single/double bonds - the first correct ring skeleton. Explains: C6H6, one monosubstitution product, three (o/m/p) disubstitution patterns. Fails: bond length 139 pm (between 154 and 134, not alternating); hydrogenation 208 vs 360 kJ/mol; substitutes instead of adding.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The ring (not the alternation) explains the isomer counts - Kekule's skeleton was right even where his bonds were wrong.
